title: the whiteboard guards have never been armed in this project
body:
# 0030: the whiteboard guards have never been armed in this project

## Tags

gates, whiteboard, false-green, hooks, upstream

## Summary

The `in-whiteboard` protocol says its timestamp rule "is enforced, not merely written down" -- a clock guard that "**refuses the commit** -- the bad stamp never lands", plus a header guard for the `key: value` block. **Neither has ever run in devbin.** This project's installed `pre-commit.intent` is the Aug 9 critic-only gate; it holds no guard roster, names no guard, and does not reference `INTENT_HOME`. Every whiteboard stamp and header block ever written here landed unchecked.

This is the cardinal class, in its purest form: not a gate that went green without examining anything, but a gate that was believed armed and was never installed. Nothing anywhere printed a word to say so.

## Reproduction

```
$ ls -la .git/hooks/pre-commit.intent
-rwx--x--x  5090 Aug  9 15:41 .git/hooks/pre-commit.intent

$ grep -cE "GUARDS|guards|roster|pre-commit-guards|INTENT_HOME" .git/hooks/pre-commit.intent
0

$ ls -la $INTENT/lib/templates/hooks/pre-commit.sh
-rwxr-xr-x 20899 Aug 21 13:31 pre-commit.sh
```

The shipped hook is four times the size and delegates its roster to `pre-commit-guards.sh`, which names `whiteboard-clock-guard.sh` and `whiteboard-header-guard.sh`. The installed one predates all of it.

**The guards themselves are fine.** Run by hand against this fold's staged content both exit 0, and the clock guard was then driven RED on purpose -- heartbeat with its trailing `Z` stripped -- and blocked with the correct `[B no Z]` diagnosis before the file was restored. So the finding is purely that nothing calls them.

## Root Cause

Guard BODIES propagate on upgrade because they are read live out of the Intent install; the ROSTER that names them lives in the copied `pre-commit.sh`, and a copy taken on Aug 9 froze a roster that did not yet exist. Intent's own shipped hook documents exactly this at its lines 49 to 67, having measured it upstream on 2026-08-20 -- the whiteboard is opt-in by directory presence, so every consumer with a board and a stale hook was "silently unguarded".

Devbin has a board and a stale hook. It is a member of the measured population that upstream already named; nothing told this project it was in the set.

## Impact

Cross-node ordering is the board's only ordering, and it is the question the inboxes exist to answer. A fabricated or local-clock stamp here is indistinguishable from a real one by inspection, so the exposure is unbounded backwards: nothing that has been committed to this project's boards has been checked, and no evidence exists either way for stamps already written.

Tonight's fold passes both guards, which is a fact about tonight's fold and about nothing before it.

No code path is affected. The critic gate that IS installed continues to work and is unaffected.

## Proposed Fix

Reinstall the hook from the current Intent so the roster arrives with it -- `intent claude upgrade`, which is also what would carry the fix for 0029's generated region. NOT done here: `/in-finish` forbids machinery changes during a session fold, the action rewrites `.git/hooks` and regenerates `CLAUDE.md`, and doing it unrequested at end of day would change the commit path in the same breath as using it.

Two things to check when it is run, neither of which the upgrade proves by itself:

- **Arm it, then drive it red before believing it.** An armed gate that has never gone red is evidence about itself. The stripped-`Z` mutation above is the cheapest red for the clock guard.
- **Ask whether the other rostered guards apply here** (`append-only-guard.sh`, `canon-ignore-guard.sh`). Arriving with the roster is not the same as being wanted; each should be a decision, not a side effect.

Worth asking separately whether a consumer should be able to detect a frozen roster at all, rather than finding out by reading its own hook 15 days later. That is Intent's question, not devbin's.

## Related

- 0029 -- the other half-upstream finding from the same fold; `intent claude upgrade` touches both
- `intent/llm/LESSONS.md` -- "What a green actually certifies"

## Resolutions

**FIXED 2026-08-25.** `intent claude upgrade --apply`, on hv's timing, after two preconditions hv set: the `_CLAUDE.md` template fix landing upstream (issue 0029) and devbin-vc's 0031 commit landing first, so the commit path was not rewritten under an active session.

**The arming, measured on the artefact rather than on the command's exit status.** The roster grep that returned **0** in the reproduction above now returns **34**; the hook went 5090 -> 20899 bytes; `intent claude upgrade` reports `CHAINED (chain block present)` where it had reported `GATE STALE`. Three of four rostered guards dispatch (`guards: 3 ran, 1 skipped`), the skip being `canon-ignore-guard`, correctly, because this project has no `intent/.canon`.

**Driven RED before being believed, all five, each restored to green.** The issue asked for the stripped-`Z` mutation; four more were added because one mutation proves one check.

| mutation                                    | result                                              |
| ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| heartbeat stamped in the future             | `[A future] ... 2307 minutes ahead of now`          |
| trailing `Z` stripped                       | `[B no Z] ... unmarked: assume LOCAL`               |
| inbox entry stamped before the one above it | `[C order] ... an append-only inbox cannot go backwards` |
| `\"` escaped quote in a header value        | refused, with the repaired line printed             |
| 20 lines deleted from `.history/`           | refused, `20 line(s) removed, 0 added`              |

**A false green was caught mid-verification, and it is the reason the later mutations look paranoid.** The header-guard mutation's anchor did not match, `str.replace` silently did nothing, and the guard returned 0 -- not because it passed a violation but because there was none to catch. It was visible only because the line was printed afterwards. Every subsequent mutation asserts its own fixture present before running, and refuses rather than proceeding if the anchor is absent.

**The critic leg was not displaced**, which is the thing an arming could most easily have broken silently: it survives at `pre-commit.intent:290` with its severity read from `.intent_critic.yml`, and it was pushed PAST its determinate-zero path (a markdown-only staged set examines nothing and says so) by running it on three real shell files.

**What the verification does NOT cover, stated because a red on one check reads as soundness about all of them.** The mutations exercise checks A, B and C's *logic*. They do not exercise the SIGPIPE race devbin-vc found at `whiteboard-clock-guard.sh:246` and `whiteboard-header-guard.sh:201` -- check B is syntactic and holds no pipeline at all -- and that race needs either >64K of added stamps or repetition under load. `intent/dc` has since fixed both guards (Intentv2 `db15e857`), driven 5/5 BLOCKED against a 170KB fixture that made the old bodies fail open 5/5.

**The guard bodies are named, because the roster is pinned and the bodies are not.** `pre-commit.sh:97` resolves `INTENT_HOME` at run time, `:145` builds the runner path from it, and `pre-commit-guards.sh:100` takes the guards as its own siblings; nothing copies a body into a consumer. So devbin's commit path changes whenever Intent's tree changes, with no commit here. The bodies these results are about: clock `42f37c2a90685812`, header `61dbbd93ab3bfa03`, append-only `fa160157f48ddf9d` -- read at arm time, and re-read after Intent committed them, byte-identical. An earlier baseline taken 15 minutes before was already stale for three of five.

**Answering the issue's own closing question:** a consumer CAN now detect a frozen roster. `intent claude upgrade` prints `GATE STALE (pre-commit.intent differs from canon; guards may not be running)` -- upstream built the detection this issue asked for. It is what named the defect on this run.

**Ruled, not a side effect:** `append-only-guard` arrives with the roster and there is no opt-out -- `pre-commit-guards.sh` gates on the `applies-when` path alone, no env var, no config, no skip list. The roster comment's "independently disabled" describes separate files, not a switch. Wanted here regardless: `.history/**` is its subject and where the 492-line loss happened.
